title: JavaScript Promises Applied Check
description: Test your ability to predict promise timing, settlement, chaining, recovery, combinator behavior, promisifying, and timeout patterns.
author: DailyCoder

questions.explanation: Promise `.then()` callbacks run asynchronously after the current synchronous code finishes.
Only the first settlement counts. Later resolve/reject calls are ignored.

questions.prompt:
What does this code log?
```js
Promise.resolve(2)
  .then((number) => number * 2)
  .then((number) => console.log(number));
```
questions.explanation: The first `.then()` returns `4`, which becomes the value for the next `.then()`.

options.text: `getOrders(user.id)` is not returned, so the next `.then()` receives `undefined`

questions.explanation: Return the Promise from `.then()` so the chain waits and passes the result onward.

options.text: Nothing; the chain stops at catch

questions.explanation: Returning a value from `.catch()` recovers the chain and passes that value to the next `.then()`.
`.finally()` does not receive the fulfilled value, and it passes the original value through.

questions.prompt: What happens when one input rejects in `Promise.all([a, b, c])`?
questions.explanation: `Promise.all()` rejects when any input promise rejects.

questions.prompt: Which method should you use when partial success is acceptable and you need every result?
questions.explanation: `Promise.allSettled()` returns an outcome for every promise, whether fulfilled or rejected.

questions.prompt: What is the main difference between `Promise.race()` and `Promise.any()`?

options.text: `race` settles with the first settled promise; `any` fulfills with the first fulfilled promise
`race` waits for all promises; `any` rejects immediately
`race` only handles arrays; `any` only handles objects

questions.explanation: `race` reacts to first success or failure. `any` ignores failures unless all promises fail.

questions.prompt: What does `Promise.any()` reject with if all inputs reject?
questions.explanation: If every input rejects, `Promise.any()` rejects with an `AggregateError`.

questions.prompt: In an error-first callback, what should a promisified wrapper do when `error` exists?

options.text: Return a string immediately from the executor

questions.explanation: Errors in callback APIs should reject the Promise, not fulfill it with an error value.

options.text: `fetch` already returns a Promise, so it can be returned directly
Promises cannot be returned from functions
`fetch` must be used only with callbacks

questions.explanation: Wrapping an existing Promise is usually the Promise constructor anti-pattern.

options.text: Settles with whichever Promise settles first

questions.explanation: `Promise.race()` settles with the first input promise that settles, fulfilled or rejected.

questions.prompt: Which API can cancel a supported `fetch` request?
questions.explanation: `AbortController` provides a signal that supported APIs like `fetch` can use for cancellation.

questions.prompt: Why should a timeout ID often be cleared in `finally`?

options.text: To clean up the timer whether the main operation succeeds or fails
To convert a Promise into a callback

questions.explanation: `finally` is a good place to clear timeout timers after an operation settles.
